Synopsis:
    A D.C. Circuit appeals court upheld an injunction blocking the Trump IRS from sharing taxpayer addresses with ICE, ruling the practice violated post-Watergate federal privacy law. The IRS had already disclosed ~47,000 records under an agreement covering up to 1.28M suspected undocumented individuals. The court found the procedure critically flawed — notably allowing fake ZIP codes to trigger disclosures — and rejected the administration's law enforcement justification.
